footer: Ember Arena — built in the browser with three.js. Assets are authored as .blend files and baked through the bounded tools/blender_bake.sh, with the browser bake as the fallback until the Blender atlas reaches parity.

versions.title: Bootstrap
versions.summary: The first browser-native arena: eight team portals, a central lava pool, 64 sprite units, a 640×360 pixel-art pass and a HUD shell.
versions.note: Independent review: 35/100. A solid pipeline baseline, but the arena is still a small blockout in a black void. M1 focuses on framing, lighting and the 32×32 octagonal layout.

versions.title: Arena Blockout
versions.summary: Dense 32×32 octagonal arena with eight radial spawn zones, a larger central lava objective, a terrain apron and a cleaner portal prefab.
versions.note: Independent review: 50/100 (M0: 35). The arena now fills the frame, the octagon and eight team gates are in place, and the HUD has a minimap, commander panel and ability grid. Remaining gaps: floor value, lava scale, unit silhouettes and portal energy.

versions.title: Simulation Core
versions.summary: Eight-team combat with waves, spatial-hash targeting, melee, arrows, crits, health bars, death states and a live battlefield HUD.
versions.note: Internal estimate ~54/100. 196 units, 164 kills, 60 draw calls and 144 FPS in the in-app browser. The art pass (M3) and VFX (M4) are next.

versions.title: Terrain Art Pass
versions.summary: Mid-value stone, a 2.5× lava basin, taller cliffs, outlying huts and unified violet portals.
versions.note: Estimated ~61/100. Bloom, damage numbers and elemental bursts landed in the next pass.

versions.title: VFX and Feel
versions.summary: Quarter-res bloom, lightning/fire/poison spells, death bursts, outlined damage text and arrow trails.
versions.note: Estimated ~64/100. 280 units at 144 FPS and 72 draw calls. HUD/minimap polish is next.

versions.title: HUD and Minimap
versions.summary: Clickable team selection, a real minimap, original SVG ability art, command grid and four central violet barriers.
versions.note: Independent review: 61/100. The minimap, altar, bloom and HUD improved, but terrain material and unit identity still hold the gate. Estimated 71-74 after the six prioritized fixes.

versions.title: Pixel-Tilemap Reboot
versions.summary: The battlefield is now a 2D 2:1 pixel-art tilemap: a 64×64 pannable map, baked flagstone and Voronoi lava, eight bases, four-direction unit sprites, authored spell sheets and a canvas pixel HUD.
versions.note: Independent review: 57/100 (M5: 61 — different medium). The pixel pivot fixed projection, 1:1 sampling, the map and the HUD; the remaining gap is art density, unit silhouettes, VFX scale and the empty plaza centre. 5 draw calls, 83 FPS at 224 units.

versions.title: Portal, Altar and Sprite Pass
versions.summary: Framed stone portals with a white-hot core now anchor the bases, a three-tier brazier-lit altar carries a faceted red crystal, and a broken-wall ruin plus mid-field ruins fill the plaza. Lava was re-keyed to dark basalt plates under broken white-hot seams, the floor ramp darkened, units rebuilt at 48×64 with 3-tone armour and team-banded shields, and the HUD skinned with an armoured portrait and a filled inventory.
versions.note: Independent review: 62/100 (M6: 57). Terrain and HUD moved; VFX is still 48, and the ice nova remains a translucent overlay that erases the units beneath it — that is the binding gap for M8.

versions.title: Gate Attempt 1: Basalt, Nova and Brass
versions.summary: Multi-scale dark basalt lava plates now sit under hot seams, the ice nova is rebuilt as an opaque, dark-outlined 14-shard burst over a scorch pool with stepped frost rings, and the fire is authored four-tone pixel art that casts light onto the ground. Team colour moved off the 2 px sash onto the cloth torso, and a wide bow silhouette makes the archer readable at 1×. The HUD gained a 5-step brass bezel, carved bronze panels, a 2× portrait, 2× icons and framed inventory slots, and a new headless `make probe` tool reports FPS, draw calls and console errors without a browser window.
versions.note: Independent review: 67/100 (M7: 62). Layout 62, Terrain 63, Units 66, VFX 63, HUD 82, Pixel art 66. HUD is the first category above 80; the gate needs 90 with no category below 80. The committed capture also absorbs the review's lava value inversion, cast light and connected nova shards, which are not re-scored.

gallery.caption: 2× detail of the altar at cam=30,30: opaque shard nova, four-tone flame and pink, teal and olive cloth torsos on the surrounding units.
Exact capture the independent 67/100 review measured; the committed m8.png is the same URL with the post-review fixes.

versions.title: Rust-Ready Reference
versions.summary: Frozen schemas, asset manifest, deterministic traces and a port plan for a Rust/WASM core.
versions.note: Planned. No Rust or networking work starts before the visual gate is signed off.

versions.title: Footmen Frenzy Match Loop
versions.summary: Units now spawn from their own barracks, team 0 selects and attack-moves them to the middle, the plaza portals are gone, and a wall ring with one gate per courtyard forces every base-to-base route through the altar. A shared map-geometry source drives both the simulation collision and the pixel tilemap; stone causeways cross the four cardinal lava pools. Every team starts with archers, buys a 150-gold swordsman upgrade, and researches a 200-gold Frenzy charge; the AI runs the same loop so the capture stays dense.
versions.note: Independent review: 72/100 (M9: 72), weighted 72.25. Layout 71, Terrain 70, Units 71, VFX 66, HUD 83, Pixel art 69. The loop's core claim is proven: no portals, one dense plaza scrum, readable gate/causeway enclosure in the west detail, and a HUD reporting gold, tier, supply and upgrade/Frenzy costs. What still binds: thinned wings/upper field, flat screen-aligned wall bricks, VFX 66. Captures are at t=25; 331 units, 5 draw calls, 60.0 FPS, console clean.

gallery.caption: West courtyard at cam=14,32: the Ember barracks door, the wall ring and gate, and a stone causeway cutting the cardinal lava pool.
2x altar detail at cam=31,31: archers and swordsmen in the central scrum, damage numerals, health bars and the nova.

versions.title: Framing, Molten Cores and the Gate
versions.summary: The scored frame now encloses the fight: an interior rampart with a ruined arch and gate sits behind the melee, so the battle reads in front of architecture rather than on an open field. Every lava field carries one offset molten core with dark crust islands, white-hot cracks and three directional flow seams, over a cooler grey floor and wider basalt plates. The west, east and north lanes gained authored ruin, conifer, crystal and brazier clumps, while the barracks-spawn, attack-move and upgrade loop from M10 is unchanged.
versions.note: Independent review: 75.2 weighted (M10: 72.25). Layout 78, Terrain 77, Units 71, VFX 67, HUD 83, Pixel art 69. The gate stays blocked on Units/VFX. Three review rounds: 73.8 → 74.6 → 75.2. Wall plinth absorbed after scoring. The most binding item is VFX: the nova is still a smooth cyan gradient web with hard white alpha-square glows, and the unit melee remains a fused-outline carpet with no front line or attack pose.

gallery.caption: The west courtyard: causeway, wall ring, barracks and the new interior rampart.
2× detail of the NW gate: ruined arch, brazier and crenellated wall run.
2× altar melee, showing the molten lava and swordsman silhouettes.

versions.title: Stepped Nova and Atmosphere
versions.summary: The altar nova is now an opaque, dark-outlined, per-pixel stepped ice star with flat value bands over a dim ground ring, and the frame is closed by a stepped edge vignette while enlarged lava embers sit alongside wing-confined dust and visible brazier, torch and gate cast pools. The altar crystal is rebuilt as a faceted, dark-outlined shard with a visible split, and the clipped alpha-square glow helpers are gone. The M10/M11 match loop, enclosure and lava craft are unchanged.
versions.note: Independent review: 77.1 weighted (M11: 75.2, +1.9). Layout 78, Terrain 77, Units 71, VFX 79, HUD 83, Pixel art 70. VFX clears the task's ≥75 bar (79). Gate still blocked on Units 71 (task 017) and VFX 79; the task's total ≥83 was unreachable from a 15%-weight category. Nova measured 750 → 15 ice colours with 2 px transitions; vignette corner/inset ratio 0.773 with every edge band darker than M11; embers 526 → 714 hot dots; gate cast light +33.9 L; no alpha squares; world 6-bit colours 736 vs M11 737. 331 units, 5 draw calls, 60 FPS, console clean.

gallery.caption: 2× altar detail at cam=31,31: the opaque stepped ice star, faceted crystal and hard value bands.
West courtyard at cam=14,32: lava embers, brazier cast pools, wall/gate craft and the stepped vignette.

versions.title: Readable Ranks and Per-Unit Fill
versions.summary: Every unit is now a single cropped quad with a tight baked contact shadow, cutting the frame from 4,528 to ~2,990 px per unit (−34%) with the feet anchor unchanged. The design cap moved 400 → 256 so the t=25 plaza holds 207 soldiers who read as ranks instead of a carpet, carried by full-face team shields, an attack/guard stance while fighting, and 11×2 green/amber/red health bars on a staggered baseline. Damage numerals stack vertically and cap at 16.
versions.note: Independent review: 78.35 weighted (M12: 77.1, +1.25). Layout 77 (−1), Terrain 77, Units 80 (+9), VFX 79, HUD 83, Pixel art 71. Units clears the 017 bar at exactly the floor, but the gate needs 90 with no category below 80, so Layout, Terrain, VFX and Pixel art still block it; the layout drop is the price of the cap and must be recovered with props, not atmosphere. Measured 60.0 FPS at the capture (221 units, 1,110 quads) and at t=92 (242 units, 1,014 quads), 5 draw calls, console clean, golden hash unchanged at 3198708409.

gallery.caption: 2× altar detail at cam=31,31: cropped single-quad soldiers with baked contact shadows, full-face team shields, staggered health bars and the guard/attack stance.
West courtyard at cam=14,32: sparse ranks and lit floor between neighbours after the 400 → 256 cap, with the wall ring, causeway and lava field unchanged.

versions.title: One-to-One World and 7×9 Numerals
versions.summary: The world now rasterizes only the HUD-visible band at 1280×481, 1:1 with no upscale, so one authored pixel is one screen pixel inside rows 47–527. Units and terrain were re-authored and drawn at 1:1, damage numerals dropped from 10×14 blocks to 7×9 cells with a 1 px rim, and the frame fell from 100% to 42.9% uniform 2×2 blocks at the 256-unit design cap. The vignette and the ramparts are baked (ADR 0012), which pays for the tier: 51–55 FPS at the t=25 capture and 58–62 FPS at the 255-unit cap on SwiftShader.
versions.note: Independent review: 80.35 weighted (M13: 78.35, +2.00). Layout 77, Terrain 79, Units 83, VFX 80, HUD 83, Pixel art 81. Task 019 bar met (Units ≥80, total ≥80); gate blocked because Layout and Terrain are below the 80 floor. The 1:1 tier is proven in pixels: uniform 2×2 blocks 100% → 42.9%, unique 5-bit colours 8,499 → 10,630 (+25%), edge share 16.3% → 20.0%. Remaining: oversized mauve floor plates, a flat baked wall, the dashed nova ring and four repeating facings (023 owns 16 facings).

gallery.caption: 2× altar detail at cam=31,31: 1:1 swordsmen with 1 px outlines, helmet brows, three steel tones and 7×9 damage numerals.
West courtyard at cam=14,32: 1:1 flagstones, the baked wall ring and causeway, and the lava field at the design cap.

versions.title: Pre-Rendered 16-Direction Units
versions.summary: Units are no longer four hand-authored facings: a procedural three.js rig (swordsman and archer) bakes to a per-team sprite atlas with 16 headings at 22.5° and idle 4 / walk 8 / attack 5 / death 6 frames, 278 frames per class, so one quad and one texture fetch carry a unit in all eight armies. Team colour is precomposed into every frame, and the swordsman reads as a shield wall while the archer reads as a hooded bowman from the front, the side and the back. The first bake was too dark to ship (Units 79, total 79.65); a value and silhouette pass lifted unit pixels L 53.1 → 76.6 and the melee dark share to 14.7% (M14 17.8%).
versions.note: Independent review: 80.10 weighted (M14 80.35). Layout 77, Terrain 79, Units 82, VFX 80, HUD 83, Pixel art 80. Task 023 clears its own bar (Units ≥80, total ≥80) and the 16-heading pipeline is accepted; the −0.25 is review-rounding, since HUD, terrain, lava and VFX are pixel-identical to M14 and the whole delta is the sprite pass. The gate is still blocked on Layout 77 and Terrain 79, both below the 80 floor at 20% weight each, and a perfect Units score could only buy ~1.4 points. The next pass is the ~10 points outside the units: task 024 composition recovery (occupy the outer thirds, clear the north-east squad from the top bar, add rim bases) and task 025 isometric ramparts with the terrain/lava rework, then a re-review. 826 quads and 5 draw calls at 207 units, 55.9 FPS at t=25 and 57.3 at the 255-unit cap on the SwiftShader probe, two cold bakes reporting rig 788eae95 / atlas a13226bd, golden sim hash unchanged 3198708409.

gallery.caption: 2× altar detail at cam=31,31: cowled archers and kite-shield swordsmen, with team capes and hoods reading at 1×.
West courtyard at cam=14,32: the wall ring and causeway behind marching archers at the design cap.
16-heading swordsman sheet with walk, attack and death rows: kite shield, wide pauldrons and crested helm.
16-heading archer sheet: rounded team cowl, thick bow with a white string and a back-view quiver.

versions.title: Composition Recovery
versions.summary: The empty east outer third is now an authored redoubt camp: a 124×212 px stone watchtower, five tents, two supply carts, three palisades, dead trees, rubble and two war banners on both shoulders of the east lane, with a wrecked siege engine and four war-kit piles bridging the 65 px gap from the rank to the camp. A two-step war memorial with a fallen crimson standard, broken swords and a brass rune closes the south approach off the lane and below the altar nova. Every new prop carries a one-canvas-pixel contour and 1 px grain on tent canvas, cart boards, palisade stakes and tower courses, plus stronger contact shadows and an AO strip under each body. The composition measure recovered with them: quiet 16×16 cells 640 → 517 and east field coverage 63.7% → 70.7%.
versions.note: Independent review: 80.90 weighted (M15: 80.10, +0.80) — the first review with every category at or above 80. Layout 80 (+3), Terrain 80 (+1), Units 82, VFX 80, HUD 83, Pixel art 80. Task 024 clears its own bar with no margin: quiet cells 517 ≤ 593, east coverage 70.74% ≥ 68.9%, Layout 80 ≥ 80. HUD, units, VFX and the west crop are pixel-identical, so the whole delta is the prop pass. Performance: 5 draw calls and 848 quads at 207 units, 53.8 FPS at the scored frame (nova active) and 59.8 FPS at the 255-unit cap on the headless SwiftShader probe, console clean, golden sim hash unchanged 3198708409. What still binds: the 92%-quiet NE strip (x 940–1150 / y 90–185 — the camp landed at y 195–470); one dark material ramp across canvas, wood and carts; prop/unit outline fusion where the wreck sits in the east rank and the memorial cuts the south rank; and the flat wall facade, mauve plates and lava seams that task 025 ramparts and the terrain/lava pass own. The remaining ~9.1 points are shared across six categories at 80–83.

gallery.caption: East redoubt at cam=38,26: the watchtower, palisade posts, A-frame tents, carts and both war banners, with the siege wreck and war litter bridging the rank to the camp gate.
West courtyard at cam=14,32: the unchanged wall ring, causeway and marching archers, pixel-identical to M15 and the control crop for the east recovery.
South memorial at cam=35,35&zoom=2: the two-step plinth, fallen crimson standard, broken swords and brass rune, drawn in front of the south rank.

versions.title: Isometric Ramparts
versions.summary: The wall ring is no longer a flat screen-space elevation: every collidable wall tile now places one isometric block with a 64×32 top diamond, only the side faces that no neighbouring wall covers, and a crest on the exposed edge, so a run along +x or +z joins as one continuous wall. Under it sits a 6 px foundation plinth with a chamfer lip, and above it a continuous 9 px merlon crest on a 3 px base course, with a broken toothed crest on ruined runs and cornices and arrow loops on towers and jambs. The gate is now a real gatehouse — a 128 px segmental arch with two voussoir courses, a broken crown with fallen blocks, a lit tunnel and two torch pools — where the tunnel is baked so units walk over it while the masonry above sorts over them. Walkway, lit face and shadow face were pulled down to L 55, L 53–57 and L 43 so the walls stop being the brightest large surface in the frame, and runs no longer read as stacked cards.
versions.note: Independent review: 82.65 weighted (M16 80.90, +1.75) — Layout 83 (+3), Terrain 85 (+5), Units 82, VFX 81 (+1), HUD 83, Pixel art 80; three passes read 82.20 → 82.10 → 82.65. Acceptance evidence: the data test asserts one rampart block per collidable wall tile from the same `mapGeometry` tiles the simulation collides with; a 1× crop shows the wall receding at 2:1 with a lit top and both faces; ring corners turn; and a unit in front of the wall draws over it while a unit behind the gate draws behind the jamb. Performance: 5 draw calls, 892 quads at 207 units (M16 848) and 854 at the 255-unit cap, SwiftShader 45.8–55.4 FPS at the scored frame (noisy software GL) and 51.4 FPS at the cap, golden sim hash unchanged 3198708409, console clean. What still binds: a comb-like merlon module, a walkway only ΔL3 above its lit face, one 1–2 px dark join at the ruin/gate tower, and the empty west-middle field; the remaining gate points are in units, VFX, HUD weight and layout, not masonry.

gallery.caption: Outer ring at cam=23,29: continuous runs with no per-tile seam, corners that turn, the 6 px foundation plinth and the continuous merlon crest.
Gatehouse at cam=27,28&zoom=2: the segmental arch with two voussoir courses, a torch-lit threshold, a broken crown with fallen blocks and the baked tunnel.
The first checkpoint pass of the same task at the scored camera (cam=32,32), kept as the before/after pair inside this milestone.

versions.title: Weight and Clarity
versions.summary: The altar nova is re-cut as ice rather than a UI starburst: five unequal arcs and four attached shards replace the dashed hoop, the 12×8 core is hollowed so floor and a unit shoulder read through it, and a single icicle bridges the void so the spell's brightest point is its centre again. A 1 px pale rim closes the silhouette, and a pruneSmallIslands pass leaves no detached sub-4 px ice fleck in the bake. Units were retuned for weight without touching the pipeline: the archer grade now lands at 0.73/1.14, team cloth at V 0.80 with a 0.66 shade step, and unlit blade, shield, bow and arrow glints give each sprite a highlight instead of the repeated cream badge, with the 16 headings and one quad per unit unchanged. The HUD slab fell from 192 px to 168 px (23.3% of the frame) and all four panels reflowed to hold their labels: minimap 224×92, portrait 64, ability grid 58×54, command card 97×30 and inventory 48×38. In the west-middle field the open floor between the colossus and the melee is now a chapel — a two-slope gable, a cross finial, a gold bell niche, an amber/ice rose window, a lit door, a crimson wall banner on the stone and a rubble apron at the plinth. The measured frame moved with it: west-middle detail 0.511 → 0.667, matched-band quiet 16×16 cells 522 → 501, world 6-bit colours 784 → 822, world mean L 65.0 → 66.4 and uniform 2×2 blocks 41.93% → 42.31%.
versions.note: Independent review: 85.75 weighted (M17 82.65, +3.10) — Layout 85, Terrain 87, Units 86, VFX 87, HUD 86, Pixel art 82; three passes read 84.55 → 85.50 → 85.75. Performance: 5 draw calls and 896 quads at 207 units (M17 892), 56.5 FPS at t=25 and 56.1 FPS at the 255-unit cap on the headless SwiftShader probe. Two cold bakes reported hash-identical rigs (9c892983 → bb726bcb), the golden simulation hash is unchanged, the console is clean and all 47 tests pass. Residual: the melee still reads as a carpet at 1×, the cream glint motif is unchanged in count, lava and wall value are untouched, and the new bottom 24 px strip is half quiet floor.

gallery.caption: 2× melee: team value at V 0.80/0.66, archer/swordsman gap 6.9 L, unlit glints.
3× west chapel: gable, cross, bell niche, rose window, rubble apron.
2× nova: broken ice arcs, four shards, hollow core with icicle, pale rim.

versions.title: Front Line
versions.summary: The melee now reads as a front line rather than an ink carpet: the near-black contour is kept while a deeper foot AO and matte V 0.64 team cloth let three ranks read on the west and south flanks with lit floor between them, and a swordsman strike lunge sits in the scored frame. The repeated cream badge is deleted rather than re-keyed — the quiver is wood and iron, and the only glint left on a rank is one short blade tip under the L163 crest rim. The bottom strip becomes a full authored band, with the supply wagon joined by broken carts, loose boards, a pennant and a palisade cut by the HUD. The ice nova gets its deep #0e2340 body back under the white shards, so the arms separate from the floor by value again.
versions.note: Independent review: 86.60 weighted (M18 85.75, +0.85) — Layout 87, Terrain 87, Units 88, VFX 88, HUD 86, Pixel art 82; the local ≥87 total is 0.40 short, and the missing point is terrain, deferred to the next milestone. Performance: 5 draw calls and 908 quads at 207 units, a clean same-state A/B of 50.1 vs 48.3 FPS at t=25, and two cold bakes that are hash-identical.

gallery.caption: 2× melee: three ranks on the flank, lit floor between them, deeper foot AO and matte cloth.
3× rank: the cream badge is gone; one short blade-tip glint and the crest rim.
3× bottom strip: supply wagon, broken carts, boards, pennant and palisade cut by the HUD.
2× nova: deep #0e2340 body under white shards, restored value separation.

versions.title: Blender Unit Forge
versions.summary: The shipped swordsmen and archers are now authored Blender files rather than a browser rig: both `.blend` sources are committed, baked through the bounded wrapper into a 16-heading sheet with idle 4 / walk 8 / attack 5 / death 6 frames per kind, and loaded by the game as 278 frame keys with no browser bake. The ingestion pass downsamples the 96×136 renders, snaps them to the shared unit palette and composites the per-team accent mask under a 1 px contour, warm rim and contact shadow, so accents take team colour while the ranks stay readable. A proportion pass — shorter shins, wider torso, shoulders and shield, a rounded shield, a taller crest — took the first 82-scoring bake through 85 back to parity at 88, equal to M19.
versions.note: Independent unit review: 88, equal to M19's 88 (Δ0; the first Blender pass read 82 → 85 → 88), so the weighted total is unchanged at 86.60 and no gate is claimed or passed. Performance: 5 draw calls and 908 quads at 207 units, 52.6 FPS at t=25 on the headless SwiftShader probe (M19 50.1 on the same box). Cost: full cold `make assets` in 20 s at 4 threads, two runs byte-identical, golden simulation hash unchanged, all 51 tests pass and the console is clean. Tile ingestion is deliberately deferred to task 028 — the stone/lava/grass/cliff sources land with the TerrainPainter value pass, while `blender/tiles/` and `bake_tile.py` sit ready.

gallery.caption: 2× melee: baked swordsman and archer frames in the crush around the ice nova — 16 headings, shaded limbs, flat team accent masks.
3× rank: three ranks of baked frames, per-team accent cloth under the 1 px contour and contact shadow.

versions.title: Terrain Value
versions.summary: The outer floor is re-keyed from grey-violet to neutral grey-brown stone, with a 20° hue mode, a 2 px dark grout and a 1 px catch-light on one-tile 64×32 plates. The rampart crest now uses a single 16 px merlon module — a 6 px merlon with a 2 px lit cap over a 3 px base course and a 10 px embrasure — and the walkway top sits warm at L 63–67, 10–14 L above its lit face. Each lava field keeps one offset molten core over a seamless 256×128 crust, with darker plates, a second shoulder lobe and hot cracks instead of a straight tile repeat.
versions.note: Independent review: 87.40 weighted (M19/M20 86.60, +0.80) — Layout 87, Terrain 90 (+3 vs M19), Units 88, VFX 88, HUD 86, Pixel art 84 (+2 vs M19); the 95 gate is still 7.6 points away, though every category is now 84–90. Measured on the scored frame: floor mauve share 18.9% → 0.8% with a 20° hue mode, the clean terrain probe reads a 0.140 saturation median, quiet 16×16 cells fall 503 → 374, the longest identical lava run drops 12 → 9 px, the walkway holds L 63–67 at ΔL 10–14 above the lit face, and the frame stays at 5 draw calls / 908 quads at 207 units with 49–54 FPS on the software probe and an unchanged golden simulation hash. Honest caveat: the full-frame saturation family still reads 0.167 because warm unit cloth and prop wood share the 20–40° gate, so the floor's neutrality is proven only on the clean probe; the next terrain point is a verified desaturation of the floor lighting, not more joint detail.

gallery.caption: 3× gatehouse crest: the 16 px merlon period with its 2 px lit cap over a 3 px base course, and the warm walkway top above the cool lit face.
2× NE lava field: the seamless 256×128 crust, one offset molten core with a hot two-lobe centre and hot cracks, and no straight tile seam.
3× outer floor: neutral grey-brown plates on a one-tile lattice, the 2 px dark grout and its 1 px catch-light, with one lighter and one darker stone step.

versions.title: HUD Craft and Blender Terrain Tiles
versions.summary: The HUD reflows to a native integer 2× grid: ability icons are 16×16 drawn at 32 px, command glyphs 16×16 inside 34 px plates, items 15×15 at 30 px, the portrait a native 64×64 and the minimap authored at its 184×92 display size, so the 168 px band carries no fractional factor at all — abilities, commands and items each measure a 1.0000 exact-2×2 share, cooldown is a bottom-up sweep over only the remaining 30% of the cycle so icons stay lit at full colour under a 1× timer chip, and the command card shows six plates with hotkey chips (U F A M H S) and a five-tone STOP ring. The terrain moved from a procedural Canvas paint to 16 authored `.blend` tiles — 6 stone, 4 lava, 4 grass and 2 cliff — built by `blender/build_tile.py`, baked through `tools/blender_bake.sh` and composited by `TerrainPainter`, with the Canvas painter retained as the fallback when the Blender atlas is absent.
versions.note: Independent review: 88.70 weighted (M21 87.40, +1.30) — Layout 87, Terrain 90, Units 88, VFX 88, HUD 91, Pixel art 87; the 95 gate is still 6.3 points away, with Layout 87 the lowest category. Four re-review passes closed every defect they raised: a stale stone bake, the grass rim/checkerboard, the unverified cliff foot, resampled review crops and a broken lava seam panel. Pass-4 shipped evidence: all 16 tiles render and are distinct in the #assets gallery (four lava variants differ by 24.2–26.2% of pixels), the grass tile-lag high-pass autocorrelation falls 0.597 → 0.066 with a 0.0 L border-to-interior delta, stone chip/fleck features rise 1,902 → 2,072 per 100k floor px with per-variant dark features 39/35/14/38/43/13 → 52/52/28/47/56/32 and pairwise-distinct crack masks, the 3×/4× detail crops are true nearest-neighbour at 1.0000 exact-block uniformity, the HUD band is 0/215,040 px different from M22, and the frame holds 5 draw calls / 908 quads at 207 units with a clean console. Residual, both bounded art tasks rather than architecture: the floor is still below the M21 value and micro-detail envelope (mean L 71.03 vs 72.30, dark share 23.5% vs 21.1%, chip features 2,072 vs 4,008 per 100k), and the lava seam patch stamps the same bright bar in the same spot on all four variants, which is visible at 2× and only a loose ~30 px rhythm at 1×.

The scored frame at 1×: the baked-tile floor reading as flagstone under the unchanged units, VFX and HUD.

versions.title: Stone Family, Map Forge and Wall Kit

The editor viewport reuses the family manifest, planDisplayTile and wallMaskAt, so authoring and play agree on every seam. The 036 wall kit is still the flat sprite set; task 043 replaces it with extruded volumes.
versions.note: This is the current M24 milestone entry, updated from planned to in-progress when task 037 shipped. The 036 release captures are preserved in the gallery. No simulation change without ?map=; the procedural arena and golden hash are unchanged. make check green with 78 tests across 12 files; console clean on the game and the editor. The 32×32 map is playable with 225 units at 5 draw calls / 604 quads. No review this task: the single feeling review stays at 042.

versions.title: Isometric Volume
versions.summary: The 16-mask wall kit and the cliff vocabulary are now extruded solids: a body, a projecting plinth, an overhanging walkway cap, individual capstones, a corner cap, and a gate/tower/ruin set, all under the fixed 2:1 three-point key.
versions.note: Task 043: 27/27 solid cells pass the volume probe (min delta top-left 15.15, left-right 21.20; 1 px #0a0b0e contour; 5.85% outline). The score is unchanged at 88.70; the single feeling review is 042.

versions.title: Second Family
versions.summary: Grass and dirt are now first-class baked families: six lawn bases with eight flower/moss/blade decals, four packed-earth bases with fifty-six dirt-to-stone and dirt-to-grass transition cells, and four earth decals, all merged with the stone sheet through one registry.
versions.note: Task 038: the painter's display lattice is material-generic and scatters family decals deterministically before the light bake; the editor previews the same cells. glade-20 is a 20x20 grass field with a stone courtyard and four dirt approaches; transitions.html proves every pair at 3x. 86 tests pass; the score is unchanged at 88.70 because the single feeling review is 042.

versions.title: Prop Library
versions.summary: A Blender-authored prop and building library replaces the flat Canvas prop row: 22 base props plus eight team variants of the banner and barracks, each an extruded solid with a fixed 2:1 camera, three-point key, 1 px contour and contact AO. The portal is now a placeable library asset.
versions.note: Task 039: `blender/props/library.blend` is baked through `tools/blender_bake.sh`, and `public/asset/props/library/manifest.json` carries footprint, anchor, team mask and face evidence. `props.html` is the proof page, and the editor and game load the same manifest. `asset_probe` reports 40/40 cells in tone order (min delta 24.44 / 15.25, outline 11.5%); 91 tests pass, and the single feeling review remains 042, so the score is unchanged at 88.70.

versions.title: Coursed Masonry
versions.summary: The extruded walls are now coursed stone instead of smooth concrete boxes: each exposed face carries staggered 6 px blocks with 1 px seams and a lit top, and an alternating quoin wraps the front corner so the masonry turns rather than stops. A continuous 5.4 px capstone rim runs the length of a wall from a shared phase, closed by a larger corner cap, while the lifted screen-right face keeps its courses legible. The result is that a wall run reads as one built wall, with individual stones and a shadow face you can actually see.
versions.note: Task 044, following the 043 extruded volume kit. `asset_probe` reports 27/27 solid cells in tone order, right face 27/27 within 44–55 (48.4–53.8), min Δ top−left 19.99 and left−right 15.24, outline 5.26%, and 4–5 courses per exposed wall face (gate 6/6, tower 5/5, ruin 4/4). The 043 smooth-box capture stays as the before image in `wallkit.html` and `volume.html`. `make check` green with 92 tests; no new review, so the single feeling review remains task 042 and the score is unchanged at 88.70.

versions.title: Unit Template and Hero
versions.summary: The unit rig was extracted out of the per-class scripts into `blender/unit_rig.py`, a shared template that both shipped classes and every future class build on. With it, a new 48x68 two-handed hero class was authored in Blender: a horned great-helm, a heavy fur mantle, spiked pauldrons, a ragged team cape and a greataxe carried in both hands. The class is proved on `units.html` with a full rank and a pure-black silhouette test, while the match atlas still holds only the two existing simulation kinds.
versions.note: Task 040. The bake carries 16 headings and idle 4 / walk 8 / attack 5 / death 6 frames in a 48x68 cell with a 96x136 gridCell, and the silhouette test renders the hero in pure black so its outline is judged without shading. `make check` is green with 93 tests, and `make probe` is unchanged at 5 draw calls / 905 quads / 207 units. Task 041's per-kind atlas is the dependency that admits the hero to gameplay, so no match code reads it yet. The single feeling review remains 042 and the score is unchanged at 88.70.

versions.title: Asset Pipeline and Per-Kind Atlases
versions.summary: Unit sprites now ship as indexed per-kind atlases composited during the bake, so the sheet page shows the real game pixels: palette-snapped colours, a 1 px contour, a warm rim and a contact shadow are burned into the texture instead of being approximated at runtime. One state table drives animation timing for idle, walk, attack and death across Blender and the renderer, so frame counts are authored and read in a single place. The match itself still fields only two kinds, Swordsmen and Archers; the hero is shipped and proved as an atlas, not yet a third kind in play.
versions.note: Task 041. The per-kind indexed atlas cuts a swordsman or archer sheet from 4.9 MB raw to 0.15 MB (~3%), with the hero at 5.2 -> 0.17 MB, and `src/data/unitPalette.json` is now the single palette source read by both `palette.ts` and `unit_rig.py`. A no-op `make assets` returns in 1.1 s and starts no Blender (32 sources skipped, 4 compositor cache hits), and two cold compositor runs are byte-identical (audit hash `a0169a229b116f048301b86e`). `make check` is green with 109 tests, and `make probe` holds 5 draw calls / 905 quads / 207 units with a clean console. The hero is a shipped kind but not yet in the match; a third match kind, and a texture-array batch if the per-kind sheets are uploaded separately, are documented in `docs/ASSET_PIPELINE.md`. A composited-vs-recomposited A/B capture differs in 145 of 921,600 pixels (0.016%, max channel delta 62) from canvas premultiplication on unit edges only, not from a change in the compositor. No score change: the score stays 88.70 and the single feeling review is task 042.

versions.title: Hero Map and the Single Feeling Review
versions.summary: A 48x48 hero arena authored in the map editor: a sealed outer wall ring, eight team courts with four lava basins, and an inner keep wall whose four cardinal gates and four corner posterns force the clash onto the central altar. The document is saved from the editor and byte-identical to the generator; a second 32x32 map is built from the same vocabulary. Authored lava runs now carry a stepped core, a dark crust rim and cast light, and the ember field follows those runs.
versions.note: Task 042. The editor shows 0 issues, 116 walls, 50 props and 8 spawns; the game capture is at seed 20261101, t=25, cam 32,32. Every category clears the 80 floor, but the total is 9.55 short of the 95 gate, so the gate is blocked and no pass is claimed. versions.title: Asset Cells and an Explicit Anchor
versions.summary: Wall, cliff and prop cells are now sized from their real projected extent plus a 1 px top and 6 px bottom margin, so a wall base draws its plinth and contact AO instead of being cut at the bitmap edge under a false dark rule. Every solid cell carries an explicit `anchorPx` and `footprint`, and walls, cliffs and props are drawn from that anchor rather than a computed height offset. A 2x2 barracks is one 160 px cell and one quad, prop draw order uses the footprint's front row, and the editor rotates a footprint with T.

Stone probe: 27/27 tone order, 27/27 right face 44-55, 27/27 frame rules, min bottom margin 8, max opaque border 0, min delta top-left 20.92, min delta left-right 16.36, outline 5.81%, 5-5 courses. versions.title: Occlusion Order
versions.summary: Walls, props, units and corpses now share one depth list, so a soldier is drawn over the masonry in front of him and clipped by the masonry behind him instead of every wall beating every unit. The terrain bitmap was cut back to the floor, its decals and its light bake; authored walls are one sprite per tile, packed from the sixteen stone family wall cells into the same atlas key space as the props. Procedural ramparts, gate jambs, the gate leaf and the gate passage are ordinary sorted sprites, and nothing solid is baked into the floor any more.
versions.note: No score change: the independent review remains 85.45, still 9.55 short of the 95 gate, so the next step is a larger art-direction pass over floor, prop and VFX craft, not another ordering fix. The sort costs about 3% median frame rate (44.1 to 42.7 FPS at 211 units, 808 to 924 quads, 5 draw calls), inside the 8% budget with the banded fallback unused.

versions.title: The Supersampling That Never Reached the Screen
versions.summary: The unit bake renders every frame on a 2x supersampled grid, but the packer reduced it with a nearest drawImage scale, so three of every four samples were discarded and each silhouette edge stair-stepped while 1 px trim and bow strings were sampled out. Task 041 had already moved the compose into the bake with an alpha-weighted area average; this pass proves it, deletes the last implicit scaling path and locks the result with a probe, a data test and a before/after view. All 278 frames of all three unit kinds recompose byte-identical to the shipped atlas, so not a sprite byte and not the atlas hash moved.
versions.note: Task 048. `downsampleArea` in src/asset-forge/palette.ts is now the one reducer (factor 2 or 3, alpha-weighted, `downsample2x` delegates to it); `composeUnitCell` accepts supersample 2 or 3 and a diagnostic `resample: 'nearest'` used by no shipped path; `WorldAtlas.readUnitCell` replaces the scaled `drawImage` in the baked-unit packer, copying a 1x cell, area-averaging a supersampled one and throwing on a non-integer ratio instead of aliasing it. Evidence from `node tools/edge_stats.mjs`: 278/278 frames per kind match the recomposed area average byte-for-byte, 0.00% semi-transparent silhouette edges (the only translucent pixels are the declared contact-shadow blob), 0 foreign alpha, and the nearest A/B still disagrees on 25-30% of boundary pixels, which `tests/data/unitEdges.test.ts` requires so a silent revert cannot pass; mean palette colours per frame are 25.3 / 24.1 / 26.3. Supersample 3 was baked once through `tools/blender_bake.sh` (nice, 4 threads) into /tmp and nothing was committed: +33% bake time (7.18 s to 9.59 s) and 2.17x the raw sheet (3.60 MB to 7.81 MB) for no measured edge gain - semi-transparency, jumps and max jump unchanged - so supersample stays 2. The 360 px internal tier the task assumed was retired in M14: the world renders 1:1 at 1280x720 and a 48x68 cell is 48x68 screen px, so the dead `INTERNAL_HEIGHT` constants in src/app/Config.ts are gone and the surviving lever is the cell itself, where doubling it costs 4x atlas memory (67.1 MB RGBA to 268 MB, an 8192^2 sheet) for no screen detail; no resolution change. The shipped atlas is untouched (`atlasHash 0b90f5c6`), `make probe` holds 5 draw calls / 971 quads / 209 units with an 888-948 ms atlas build, `make check` is green with 143 tests, the console is clean and the golden sim hash is unchanged because no simulation code was touched. No score change: the last independent review remains 86.50 (task 047), 8.50 short of the gate, and this task does not re-score.

3x melee crop from the scored frame: 1 px contours, team edges and armour trim arrive intact from the area-average cell, with no resample step on the silhouette.
the scored world frame at seed 20261101, t=25: identical art and identical atlas bytes, proving the fix removed a defect without reopening the reviewed look.

highlights: Nearest reduction gone from every shipped path; `downsampleArea` is the one reducer
278/278 frames per kind recompose byte-identical to the shipped atlas
0.00% semi-transparent silhouette edges, 0 foreign alpha; nearest A/B still differs on 25-30%
Supersample 3 baked once: +33% time, 2.17x raw sheet, no edge gain - stays 2
World is 1:1 at 1280x720; 360 px tier retired, dead constants removed, no resolution change

versions.title: Unit Redesign: Helmets, Glowing Eyes and a Real Gait
versions.summary: The swordsman and archer are re-authored in Blender so the head is roughly a third of the figure instead of a pylon on a box body, the face is a dark visor slit with two glowing eyes, the shield and recurve bow are larger, and the walk is a real four-beat gait - a knee that bends and trails, a hip drop on each foot strike, a counter-rotating torso and an opposite arm swing - instead of a pendulum of straight legs. Idle adds a weight shift, attack a bigger wind-up. Two cold bakes are byte-identical, 143 tests pass and the simulation hash is unchanged.

The Flash loop's earlier unit attempt (049) was parked in git stash@{0} and left in place. blender/build_unit.py enlarges the bucket helm and hood to 0.34 wide with a dark face and glint eyes, enlarges the kite shield and recurve bow, and rewrites idle/walk/attack keyframes for weight, a planted foot and a counter-rotating torso. Geometry and keyframes only: no palette, atlas, cell, resolution or simulation change; the bake runs through tools/blender_bake.sh and check_assets verifies the .blend hashes.
